Species habitat dictionary for OCS-GE land cover and land use

Source: R/data.R
ocsge_species_dict.Rd

Habitat suitability, breeding, foraging and movement scores of 935 European terrestrial vertebrates (amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals) for the French OCS-GE nomenclature: the 14 cover classes (CS), and 47 (cover, use) pairs for which the land use (US) changes what the cover stands for. It has the same columns as eunis_species_dict, plus code_us.

Usage

data(ocsge_species_dict)

Format

A data frame with 57,035 rows (935 species x 61 classes) and 14 columns:

code_cs

Character. OCS-GE cover code, as in ref_ocsge$code_cs (e.g. "CS2.2.1").

code_us

Character. OCS-GE use code (e.g. "US1.1"), or NA on the rows giving the scores of the cover whatever its use.

species_name

Character. Scientific name, genus and species separated by "_".

sppID

Character. Species identifier from the EEA source table; the first letter gives the group (A, R, B, M).

taxon_group

Character. "amphibian", "reptile", "bird" or "mammal".

suitability

Integer (0-10). Overall habitat suitability: 0 unused or avoided, 2 marginal, 5 secondary, 8 main, 10 core habitat.

weight_breeding

Integer (0-10). Value of the class as a breeding, nesting, denning, roosting or larval site.

weight_foraging

Integer (0-10). Value of the class for feeding.

permeability

Integer (0-10). Ease of movement through the class: 10 moves freely, 7 readily, 4 reluctantly, 1 strong barrier, 0 impassable. Accounts for flight, swimming or fossorial habits.

resistance

Numeric (1-100). Derived from permeability as 10^(2 * (1 - permeability / 10)): 10 gives 1, 5 gives 10, 0 gives 100.

habitat_breadth

Integer. Species-level: number of cover classes (out of 14) with suitability >= 5.

specialization

Numeric (0-1). Species-level: 1 minus the normalised Shannon evenness of the suitability profile over the 14 cover classes (0 generalist, 1 specialist).

confidence

Integer (1-3). Species-level: 1 vague or missing source description, 2 medium, 3 detailed.

in_france

Integer (0/1). Species-level: 1 if the species occurs natively and regularly in metropolitan France (expert knowledge). The dictionary covers Europe while OCS-GE covers France: filter on this column first.

Details

Cover rows (code_us = NA, 935 x 14). Scores were assigned by a large language model (Claude Opus 5.5) reading the EEA habitat and avoided-habitat descriptions of each species against an ecological description of each cover class, with the anchored rubric given above.

Cover x use rows (935 x 47). They are derived, not scored again: each (cover, use) pair is linked to one or several EUNIS Level 2 classes by ref_ocsge_eunis, and takes the mean of their eunis_species_dict scores weighted by 1 / rank. For instance herbaceous cover under agricultural use (CS2.2.1, US1.1) is mostly arable land (I1, rank 1) but may be permanent grassland (E2, rank 2). Only the pairs listed in ref_ocsge_eunis have a row; for any other pair use the cover row, which is what join_ocsge_species does.

These are expert-judgement scores and have not been validated against occurrence data. They were checked against the keywords of the EEA habitat, avoided-habitat and threat descriptions (raw_data/check_ocsge_species_dict.R of the source repository): species naming a habitat score higher on the matching class than the others, with a probability of 0.57 to 0.93 depending on the habitat for cover rows, and 0.68 to 0.93 for cover x use rows. The use helps most for gardens and parks (0.57 to 0.80), quarries (0.69 to 0.93) and arable land (0.74 to 0.77).

Change from spacemodR 0.3.0. The dictionary used to hold scores from another model for the cover classes only, in the columns weight_global, weight_movement, weight_foraging and resistance (1-10), with nom_espece and cover codes written with a space ("CS 2.2.1"). suitability replaces weight_global and permeability replaces weight_movement; values differ (Spearman correlation 0.72 for suitability, 0.22 for movement, mostly because flying species were scored as if they walked) and are lower on classes that are not habitat.

References

The species list and the habitat descriptions come from:

O'Connor, L. M. J., Renaud, J., Dou, Y., Karger, D. N., Maiorano, L., Verburg, P. H., & Thuiller, W. (2024). Habitat Suitability of European Land Systems for Terrestrial Vertebrates. Global Ecology and Biogeography, 33(11), e13903.

See also

join_ocsge_species, ref_ocsge, ref_ocsge_eunis, eunis_species_dict

Examples

data(ocsge_species_dict)
apsy <- subset(ocsge_species_dict, species_name == "Apodemus_sylvaticus")

# scores of each cover, whatever its use
subset(apsy, is.na(code_us), c(code_cs, suitability, permeability, resistance))
#>         code_cs suitability permeability resistance
#> 55877 CS1.1.1.1           5            4       15.8
#> 55879 CS1.1.1.2           2            1       63.1
#> 55880 CS1.1.2.1           2            2       39.8
#> 55887 CS1.1.2.2           0            1       63.1
#> 55888   CS1.2.1           3            3       25.1
#> 55891   CS1.2.2           0            0      100.0
#> 55898   CS1.2.3           0            0      100.0
#> 55899 CS2.1.1.1           8            9        1.6
#> 55906 CS2.1.1.2           8            9        1.6
#> 55912 CS2.1.1.3           8            9        1.6
#> 55918   CS2.1.2           9           10        1.0
#> 55921   CS2.1.3           8            9        1.6
#> 55922   CS2.2.1           8            9        1.6
#> 55937   CS2.2.2           2            4       15.8

# herbaceous cover, by use
subset(apsy, code_cs == "CS2.2.1", c(code_us, suitability, weight_foraging))
#>       code_us suitability weight_foraging
#> 55922    <NA>           8               8
#> 55923   US1.1           8               8
#> 55924   US1.2           9               9
#> 55925   US1.3           5               5
#> 55926     US2           9               9
#> 55927   US235           8               8
#> 55928     US3           8               8

#> 55930 US4.1.2           6               6
#> 55931 US4.1.3           6               6
